evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'I just need ten to fifteen minutes of your time. Is this a good time?' but does not frame a 'dependable quote' promise or wait for a clear yes — customer only says 'Mm-hmm' and 'Yeah, that's fine,' which is rushed past.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks 'aside from the pack, aside from the pricing, do you have any other concerns about the moving process?' — but this comes after already confirming the address, so probing has technically begun.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about measuring furniture to fit through doors and then asks about disassembly fees. Rep answers the disassembly question ('already included in hourly rate') but never asks 'tell me more' or explores the underlying concern about fit. Acknowledged, one-layer response, move on.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No recap of concerns. Rep moves directly from the disassembly answer into 'So, for now again this is a $800 square feet...' without reflecting back what was heard.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (1BR apt), floor/stories (6th floor with elevator), rooms (bedroom, living room), walking distance (100+ feet from parking), special considerations (freight elevator reservation, plant liability waiver, furniture pieces: queen bed, 65" TV, desk, monitors, bedside tables). Additional stop (destination address confirmed as 1BR first-floor apt with ~100 feet to parking). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep asks 'it says here that you need packing services. When you say packing it's us putting everything in two boxes. Would you okay.' Customer replies 'No, I don't need that.' Offered and declined.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asks 'normally for a one bedroom apartment receive fifth fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?' Asked and confirmed ~15–25 boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides hourly rate ($111/mover, 2 movers = $222/hr), includes gas/insurance/pads/tools, no hidden fees, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments. Then personalizes: 'in your case, we're coming from a sixth floor apartment with reserved elevator and a long walk, going to a first floor apartment... So I estimate the move to finish in three and a half to four and a half hours.' Final estimate: $777–$999. Both range and personalization present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses hourly rate, two movers, all-inclusive framing (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wraps, pads, tools, disassembly/reassembly). Explicitly states 'no heat fees' (likely 'no hidden fees'). Covers 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments. Full transparency and commitment framing present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent check-in after the $777–$999 estimate. Rep immediately pivots to 'And then if you want we can proceed on scheduling you for October 31st Saturday' without pause.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Not mentioned. No reference to a discount if late or any on-time promise.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not mentioned. No reference to $2,000 coverage, no-deductible framing, or damage coverage built into the rate.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No Two Promises section delivered at all; closing loop cannot be assessed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep goes straight to 'And then if you want we can proceed on scheduling you for October 31st Saturday. We do not require any deposit.' No version of 'What's still concerning you?' or genuine final check-in.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep says 'if you want we can proceed on scheduling you' — framed as optional, not a direct 'Would you like our help with your move?' The customer declines to book ('I'm gonna wait') and rep accepts, offering only 'I can just send everything to your email.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep states 'We do not require any deposit' — deposit policy mentioned, rate-lock framing not explicitly stated but implied by no-deposit commitment.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep does NOT confirm: date (assumes Oct 31 but no final confirmation of readiness), phone number (not collected), arrival window (not discussed), crew size (mentioned 'two movers and one truck' in estimate but not re-confirmed at close), addresses (confirmed during probing but not re-confirmed at booking), or notes for crew (not left). Only pickup address (3255 Carlisle) and destination address (2787 North Houston) were already confirmed during discovery.

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details (floor, elevator, distances, furniture inventory, plant liability) with systematic questioning, and delivered a properly anchored, personalized estimate ($777–$999) with full fee transparency and minimum/increment framing.
coaching_note: Jeline skipped the entire Two Promises section (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) and never asked for the business directly — after the customer said 'I'm gonna wait,' she accepted immediately without attempting to address remaining concerns or close; she must deliver both promises on every full-sales call and use a clear 'Would you like our help?' ask, then pause for the answer before pivoting to logistics.
